terms.definition: The annual cost of borrowing money expressed as a percentage, including interest rates and upfront fees charged by lenders.
terms.example: A $5,000 credit card balance with a 24% APR accrues approximately $100 in interest in the first month alone.

terms.definition: The real rate of return earned on a savings account or investment over one year, taking into account the compounding effect of interest.
terms.example: A High-Yield Savings Account with a nominal 4.5% rate compounded daily yields a 4.60% APY.

terms.definition: Interest calculated on both the initial principal deposit and all accumulated interest from previous periods ('interest earning interest').
terms.example: $10,000 invested at 8% annual return doubles to over $21,500 in 10 years without adding another penny.

terms.definition: The percentage of your gross monthly income that goes toward paying fixed monthly debt obligations.
terms.formula: DTI = (Total Monthly Debt Payments / Gross Monthly Income) × 100
terms.example: If your gross income is $6,000/mo and your debt payments are $1,800/mo, your DTI is 30%. Lenders prefer a DTI below 36%.

terms.definition: The proportion of your revolving credit limits currently in use. Highly influential in FICO credit score algorithms.
terms.formula: Utilization = (Total Credit Card Balances / Total Credit Limits) × 100
terms.example: Carrying a $1,500 balance across a total credit line of $5,000 represents a 30% utilization ratio.

terms.definition: The scheduled repayment of a loan through regular periodic installments, gradually shifting from heavy interest payments toward principal payoff.
terms.example: In Year 1 of a 30-year mortgage, over 70% of each monthly payment goes to interest. By Year 25, over 80% goes toward principal.

terms.definition: The total invested net worth required to sustain your lifestyle indefinitely without relying on active employment, traditionally based on the 4% Safe Withdrawal Rate rule.
terms.example: If your household spends $60,000 annually, your baseline FIRE target is $1,500,000 ($60,000 × 25).

terms.definition: Marginal tax is the rate applied to your highest tax bracket dollar. Effective tax rate is the actual average percentage of total income paid to taxes.
terms.formula: Effective Tax Rate = (Total Tax Owed / Gross Income) × 100
terms.example: An individual in the 22% marginal federal tax bracket may only have an effective federal tax rate of ~12.8% due to standard deductions and progressive brackets.
